reasoning: The proposal's exact research question and method are directly addressed by "Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels" (arXiv 2605.29800), which runs multiple LLM judges across NLI benchmarks with ground truth, quantifies error correlation via Kish effective sample size against a Condorcet independence null, and finds actual majority-vote accuracy falls 8-22 percentage points short of the independence ideal with ~75% of nominal independence lost to shared mistakes — precisely the "inflation under the independence assumption" the proposal aims to measure. Multiple adjacent works reinforce this: "Correlated Errors in Large Language Models" (arXiv 2506.07962), CARE (arXiv 2603.00039), and Hierarchical Family Voting all document correlated judge errors defeating majority-vote aggregation and even propose mitigations. The proposal's "vary same model across prompts/temperatures" wrinkle adds only marginal novelty over this body of work, and the temperature-vs-error-rate relationship is itself already mapped (arXiv 2603.28304); the core problem — measuring correlated judge errors and the resulting overstatement of aggregated-oversight accuracy — is solved.

evidence.title: Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels
evidence.summary: Runs 9 LLM judges across 7 families on NLI benchmarks with ground truth; uses Kish effective sample size and a Condorcet independence null to show actual panel accuracy falls 8-22 points short of the independent-voting ideal, with ~75% of nominal independence lost to correlated errors and the best single judge matching or beating the panel. This is essentially the proposed study.

evidence.title: Correlated Errors in Large Language Models
evidence.summary: Documents systematic, correlated errors across LLMs and the consequences for ensemble/judge aggregation, directly establishing that judge errors are not independent and that aggregation does not wash them out.

evidence.title: CARE: Confounder-Aware Aggregation for Reliable LLM Evaluation
evidence.summary: States that LLM judges exhibit correlated errors from shared latent confounders, causing majority vote/averaging to give little gain or amplify mistakes; proposes a fix evaluated on 12 benchmarks. Confirms the problem (and a solution) is already published.

evidence.title: The Necessity of Setting Temperature in LLM-as-a-Judge
evidence.summary: Shows temperature is strongly correlated with judge error rates and agreement, covering the proposal's 'vary the same model under temperatures' angle for inducing/measuring judge error variation.

evidence.title: Auditing Multi-Agent LLM Reasoning Trees Outperforms Majority Vote and LLM-as-Judge
evidence.summary: Demonstrates majority vote and LLM-as-judge are undermined by correlated agent behavior and proposes an alternative, reinforcing that the limitations of naive aggregation under correlated errors are an active, addressed research area.
